Everyone's saying "PSF prices are crazy high" - yet 2025 saw the highest new launch sales since 2021.

What do these buyers know that you don't? 📊

The secret? 🧐 

PSF numbers are misleading due to recent regulatory changes. 

Smart buyers focus on total quantum, not just PSF.

For condo upgraders and HDB MOP owners building toward a S$5M portfolio: There are still well-priced units available TODAY with excellent layouts. Don't let PSF headlines fool you into missing this opportunity.

BUT, this pricing window won't last forever. 😳

Recent land bids have come in at EVEN higher prices - meaning next year's launches will be genuinely more expensive. ‼️

headline: "PSF Too High" - Yet Record Sales? Here's Why
transcript_text: PSF prices are too high, so how much more can they increase by? This is what I hear on the ground. But here's the part that most people miss. Why was it that new launch sales last year was the highest since 2021, which was post-COVID where interest rates were also low? Aren't all these buyers also concerned about the high per square foot prices? Let's take for example the River Valley area. These are the average per square foot prices transacted in the past six months. Yes, per square foot numbers for new launches such as Promenade Peak, River Green and Zion Grand look higher. But when we convert it into the total cost per unit, here is where it gets different. The average cost of a three-bedder unit for the new launches was comparable or even cheaper than some of the resale properties such as Riviere and Martin Modern. with arguably better locational attributes since they are nearer to Great Wall City. So measuring per square foot alone will not give you the full picture since the way that per square foot is measured has changed with the years due to regulations such as the GFA harmonization introduced most recently which removes aircon ledges from total sellable area Naturally when the sellable area gets smaller the per square foot prices go up However the overall quantum buyers are paying is often similar to what they would have paid before, sometimes even lower, which is why launch day sales for these projects were hot. This is one key reason why people are still buying despite the headlines. So what's important is to understand that this window of opportunity will not last forever. Recent land bids have been coming in at significantly higher costs. As those projects launch, developers won't have the same flexibility on pricing. This means that per square foot prices and quantum for projects later this year and into 2027 are unlikely to look like today's. But thankfully, there are still available units in the market which have decent layouts and are at today's more affordable prices. Don't wait until this window of opportunity closes. If you're considering buying private property and want to understand how current pricing actually translates to real dollars, not just per square foot headlines, let's sit down and have a proper discussion. Book an appointment with me by clicking the link below and I'll walk you through how this applies to your situation.
